clue.text: In the right set, with water supply ensured?

explanation.surface: Someone moves in the best circles and has a reliable water main too.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well placed socially means having influential friends; literally, a house hooked up to the mains has its supply assured.

clue.text: State of the floating pound?

parts.note: a currency allowed to float suggests economics, but a pound is also a measure of mass, and floating free means having no heaviness

explanation.definitionFit: The condition of having no apparent heaviness, as when drifting in orbit.

clue.text: See one learner copy another, making part of coat

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
to ape is to copy
a second learner, another L

explanation.surface: A student watches one pupil imitate another, while making a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The folded flap below the collar on the front of a jacket.

clue.text: E.g. muggers of school-kids out for a walk

explanation.surface: Street robbers target pupils on an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: The mugger is an Indian species of reptile; a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs is also called by this name in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Mugger is a kind of large reptile with jaws; pupils walking two by two in a file form one too.

clue.text: Such a striking activity is catching

explanation.surface: Hitting things turns out to be infectious.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammering in pins is a striking job; catching a culprit is pinning them down.

clue.text: It would be most ingenious to get 150 over this mountain

indicators.note: the clue says this mountain would become the clever word once the number is placed over it, so the number is what to remove

parts.note: the cleverest is the most ingenious
CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Climbing the world's highest peak with a heavy load would be a brilliant feat.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse-style clue: 'It would be' says the mountain plus the Roman numeral placed over it makes 'most ingenious'; 'to get' and 'over' describe that placing.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest peak, in the Himalayas.

clue.text: 12 changes in sentence

indicators.note: the letters of 12's answer are changed about into a new order

parts.note: 12-across is the four-letter bit of news

explanation.surface: A list of amendments to a prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison sentence is the period a convict spends inside, as in 'doing porridge'.

clue.text: Commands for volunteers, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the volunteers are placed in the manner of speaking, inside it

parts.note: diction is a manner of speaking
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Orders given to recruits, in some sense of the phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer force.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictating means issuing orders authoritatively, so laid-down orders or prescriptions.

clue.text: Decisive defeat at game between London banks

parts.note: Napoleon's final defeat at Waterloo gives the phrase 'meet one's Waterloo'
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A crushing loss at a sport played between City financial institutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' look like City finance houses, but they are the riverbanks of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A road crossing spanning the Thames in central London, linking its two shores.

clue.text: Play, unrehearsed, is better outside

indicators.note: the word for better sits outside, wrapping round the little word is

parts.note: to better something is to improve it
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unscripted performance is judged superior to a rehearsed one.
explanation.definitionFit: To play without rehearsal is to extemporise, making it up on the spot.

clue.text: After short time, supply tea or coffee

indicators.note: the tea word is placed after the short time, coming second

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a short time
CHA is slang for tea

explanation.surface: After a brief wait, a caterer offers a choice of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate-flavoured or Arabian variety of the drink served in cafes.

clue.text: Chap will ring — and probably hear this

parts.note: HE stands for a chap, a man
'LL is the contracted form of will
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A man is going to phone, and you can guess what he will be greeted with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap will' together is the contraction HE'LL; the ring is the telephone's as well as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual greeting when picking up a ringing telephone.

clue.text: Bit of news producing some excitement

indicators.note: only some of the word excitement is taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A news snippet stirs up a little excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: A single report or article in a newspaper or bulletin.

clue.text: Girl of 19

parts.note: 19's answer read as a single word followed by 'off' tells you to scramble that word, giving a girl's name

explanation.walkthrough: 19-down is TAKE-OFF: read it as TAKE, 'off', with off as an anagram signal, and the four letters rearrange to a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of Katherine, a common female first name.

clue.text: In US money, about a third of remaining profits

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the US coins go about the piece, surrounding it

parts.note: cents are American money

indicators.note: the first three of the nine letters of remaining, a third of the word

explanation.surface: In dollar terms, roughly a third of what is left is profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a third of' takes the opening three of the nine letters; 'about' wraps the coins round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Gains or additions, amounts by which something grows.

clue.text: Making cuts in private education here?

explanation.surface: Budget cuts are being made to a fee-paying school.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCING College is a fee-paying boarding school in West Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting open with a blade is piercing a boil; the other sense is a well-known English independent school.

clue.text: Place of entertainment for one in evening suit?

explanation.surface: A venue for someone in a dinner jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like formal wear, but it is a card suit: a club played after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue for late drinking and dancing; jokingly, a card of the clubs suit for the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Illustrator requires lenient treatment

indicators.note: the letters of the word lenient are given treatment, worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist asks to be dealt with gently.
explanation.walkthrough: John TENNIEL drew the original pictures for Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Tenniel was the Victorian artist famous for drawing Alice in Wonderland and Punch cartoons.

clue.text: Split up FBI agents in group

indicators.note: the agents are placed in the group word, inside it

parts.note: a set is a group
G-men are FBI agents (government men)

explanation.surface: Federal agents are divided up within a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To segment is to divide into sections, breaking something apart.

clue.text: Opposite of a landing strip

explanation.surface: The reverse of an airstrip landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landing strip' looks like one phrase, the runway, but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft departing is the reverse of arriving; to remove clothing is to undress.

clue.text: Foul-spoken method of preparation for battle

explanation.surface: A fighting technique accompanied by foul language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul-spoken' means 'fowl' said aloud: chicken MARENGO is a classic dish, named after Napoleon's 1800 victory over the Austrians.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of cooking chicken, said to have been invented after a battle Napoleon won in northern Italy.

clue.text: One who looks after silver in half-hearted fashion?

indicators.note: silver is placed in the shortened word, inside it
the heart of the fashion word is its double letter, and half of it goes

parts.note: manner and fashion both mean way
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A butler polishes the family silver without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' halves the doubled middle letter pair of the fashion word, leaving MANER; 'in' puts the silver symbol inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in charge who runs or supervises things.

clue.text: Observe Lawrence's initial disappearance

parts.note: NO marks an absence, as in 'no one there'
T.E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by the initials T.E.

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a person called Lawrence has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'no T.E.': Lawrence's initials have disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe something is to take notice of it or remark on it.

clue.text: Hide swindle

explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its pelt; to fleece someone is to cheat them of money.

clue.text: Relatively close finisher of game?

explanation.surface: A relative who wraps up the match at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: MATER is Latin for mother, a close relative; with a question mark it is also one who mates, ending a chess game.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother is the nearest of kin; checkmate ends chess, so one who delivers it finishes the game.

clue.text: Opera — turning up thus in third part of it

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up reads the whole assembly from bottom to top
the word for thus is placed in the act, inside it

parts.note: an opera is divided into acts, the third being one part
so means thus

explanation.surface: An opera singer appears in the third act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' makes ACSOT, and 'turning up' reverses it, as suits a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's tragic opera about a singer, set in Rome.

clue.text: Not the contrary girl who arranges army quarters

indicators.note: the word army is arranged, its letters put into another order

explanation.surface: A girl who isn't contrary sorts out the soldiers' billets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' girl is Mary from the nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary', whose name also uses these letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's first name, a rearrangement of the rhyme's Mary but not her.

clue.text: Vehicle resentfully withdrawn

explanation.surface: A car is pulled out of service amid bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled horse cart for one person, used in harness racing; also moody and sullen.

clue.text: Grandiose trip arranged

indicators.note: the letters of Grandiose stumble, tripping into a new order

explanation.surface: An extravagant holiday has been booked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put in order or planned in advance has been sorted out.

clue.text: WWII plane has to climb — doesn't go above Hurricane

parts.note: the Bristol Beaufort was a British torpedo bomber of the Second World War
to scale a wall is to climb it

explanation.surface: A fighter plane must gain altitude but stays lower than a Hurricane fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hurricane looks like the other fighter plane, but it is the top of the wind-force table, force 12.
explanation.definitionFit: The wind-force measure runs from 0 (calm) to 12, its top rating being hurricane force.
